data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03's countercondition admits that an engine can 'generate a formal counter-example that contradicts its own initial claim through deterministic execution,' which concedes that a single engine CAN identify its own errors under the right procedure. But the main claim asserts separation is 'necessary' because shared priors 'prevent' a single model from identifying its own systemic hallucinations. The countercondition is not merely an edge case; it directly negates the necessity claim by demonstrating a mechanism by which same-engine verification succeeds. The target thus internally undermines its own position without reconciling the tension.
